Standard notarial acts

I’ll walk you through each step in English or Spanish, whichever you prefer.

$15 max per act

Acknowledgments

You tell me, in person, that you signed the document of your own free will.

$15 max per act

Oaths & affirmations (jurats)

You swear or affirm in front of me that what the document says is true, and then you sign.

$15 max per act

Signature witnessing

I check your ID and watch you sign in person.

$15 per copy

Copy certifications

I certify that a copy of your document is true to the original: diplomas, passports, IDs and out-of-state records. I can’t certify Colorado vital records or that a person is alive. What I can and can’t certify.

Part 2 of 3

Specialized & travel services

When a document is leaving the country, gets signed at the airport, or needs more than a stamp.

Signatures only

Minor travel consent letters

I notarize parents’ or guardians’ signatures on travel consent letters, often needed for trips to Latin America. You bring the letter already written; I don’t write it or give legal advice. If you need it in Spanish too, I can translate it.

$95 flat+$10 per signature

Denver airport (DIA)

I’ll meet you inside the terminal. It’s a flat $95, parking included, plus $10 for each signature I notarize. How it works.

For title companies

Loan signings

Purchases, refinances, and HELOCs. The title company sends me the package and I meet you to sign it. I only print the package; I don’t prepare it. For business.

From $30 per page

Certified translations

I translate personal and official documents between Spanish and English, and sign a certification with each one. Prices & bundles.

If your attorney gave you instructions

If your attorney, here or abroad, told you how the notarization needs to look, bring those instructions to the appointment. I notarize under Colorado law; what the other country requires is for your attorney or the receiving agency to decide.

🌐 Colorado Secretary of State Apostilles

Four options: Full-Service (I notarize and deliver; local only, from $150), Local Denver Courier ($85), and Statewide Expedited Courier ($115) for documents that are already notarized. Living abroad? There’s also International Remote ($180). I hand-deliver everything to the Secretary of State.

Office & employer services

Work that doesn’t need a notary seal, for employers and individuals. Government forms are free; my fee covers typing and my time.

No notary seal

I-9 employment verification

I can act as your authorized representative to look at your new hire’s documents and complete Section 2 of Form I-9. Pricing.

Forms are free from the government

U.S. passport form help

I type your answers into the DS-11 or DS-82 form and, if you’d like, go with you to your appointment to help with the language. I charge only for typing and my time. Options & pricing.

Forms are free from the government

DMV paperwork

I help you get your papers in order before you go to the DMV, so you don’t get turned away for something missing. I charge only for typing and my time. For full DMV paperwork help, visit Ayuda DMV.

Before your appointment

What to bring

  • ✓Your ID: a passport, driver’s license, or other government ID that’s current or expired no more than one year.
  • ✓The document, filled out: everything except the signature and date. You’ll add those in front of me.
  • ✓Language: I can notarize documents in any language, but the notarial certificate (the part I sign) will be in English, as Colorado law requires.

What I can’t do

  • ✗Explain legal terms or tell you what a contract means.
  • ✗Pick which type of notarization you need. The agency or person receiving the document will tell you.
  • ✗Fill in blanks or fix mistakes on your forms.

How I work

Commissioned & insured

I’m a Notary Public commissioned in Colorado (ID 20254044224). Servicios Quintana LLC is insured through The Hartford: general liability, data breach, and professional liability (errors & omissions) for my notary and translation work. If you need a certificate of insurance, just ask.

AI disclosure

I sometimes use artificial intelligence as an office tool to help organize or translate documents. I review and edit every result and do everything in my power to make it correct; I’m human and can make mistakes, and if you find one, I’ll fix it. I never put your personal information (Social Security numbers, addresses, and so on) into public AI systems.
